rationale: OWNER RULING, 2026-08-08, on architecture_review/RFC_017: flip the completion-verifier registry from fail-OPEN to fail-CLOSED on verifier error, with a per-verifier opt-out. This is the execution of a decision already taken, not a proposal — what is under review is whether the implementation is the right shape, not whether the flip should happen. The ruling was taken on a measurement this lane produced the same day, and the measurement is the whole argument. Before it, every registered verifier failed OPEN: a verifier returning an error meant 'verification could not run at all', and CompleteWorkItemAction stamped the item 'complete' anyway, recording the error under result._verification. That policy was stated in a doc comment (verifiers.go) and inherited by all 8 registered verifiers, present and future. Its stated justification was that discovery re-detection plus the two-strike rule is the backstop. Measured over the registry's entire life (gate live since e1b8e1f84, 2026-07-14): verifiers have errored TWICE, out of 11 consultations ever. Both errors were empty_section's absent-target branch. On BOTH, the page still declared the slot in pages.sections, which is precisely the disambiguator bugs_closed/032 named for telling a legitimate removal from a deletion - so the honest verdict was Resolved:false on both, and fail-open stamped both 'complete' at attempt_count 0. Five days later no re-detection had followed, although findEmptySections' own predicate, run verbatim, still returns both components (deployed, unlocked, unsuppressed - so bugs_open/185's deployed-only blindness is not the explanation) and the check demonstrably ran on that site four times afterwards, retracting 10 other items. The backstop missed the only two cases it has ever been asked to catch, and the defect is live on two production pages today. Zero of the errors were infrastructural: no DB blip, no timeout, no malformed spec. The transient-failure case fail-open exists to protect against has never once been observed, while the case it demonstrably mishandles has occurred 100% of the time it fired. The owner also explicitly declined RFC_017's option 2 (a lint forbidding error-returns for non-infrastructural cases): under fail-closed an error return means 'do not complete', which is the safe direction, so the guard largely evaporates. And option 3 (a third Indeterminate outcome that parks the item without burning attempts) was explicitly NOT taken - it is the structural answer and remains open in RFC_017, but the owner chose the cheap reversible flip first, with the wasted-retry cost as the evidence that would later justify the bigger change. That cost is real and is named in the risks block rather than hidden.

plan.summary: The ItemVerifier registry fails OPEN on error: a verifier that cannot run completes the work item anyway. Measured, that path has fired twice in the registry's life and was wrong both times, while the transient-failure case it protects has never been observed. Per owner ruling on RFC_017, flip the default to fail-CLOSED - an error now routes the item into the same attempt machinery as a persisting defect - and make the old behaviour reachable only through an explicit per-item_type opt-in field whose unsafe default is OFF, per the owner's 2026-08-02 shared-seam ruling. RegisterVerifier keeps its signature so all 8 existing registrations silently become safe; GetVerifier now returns the policy alongside the verifier so a caller cannot consult one while forgetting the other. Two collateral correctness fixes ride with it because the flip exposes them: the blocked-completion message was hard-coded to claim the defect was found still present and read its text from a key the error payload does not have, and the policy branch had no test because it was only reachable through a live database.

edits.rationale: Make the failure policy a registration-time field with the unsafe default OFF, rather than a global behaviour licensed by a doc comment. The 2026-08-02 owner ruling on shared seams is explicit that authority of this kind ships as an opt-in field, not a documented contract, because a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share - and this is the exact shape it describes: the previous fail-open authority was invisible to any reviewer reading a calling check. RegisterVerifier's signature is deliberately unchanged so the flip reaches all 8 existing registrations without editing 8 files, and the zero VerifierPolicy is the safe one, so both an unregistered type and a caller that ignores the new return value land on the safe branch.

Apply the policy, and split the decision out as a pure function. The split is not tidiness: the fail-open/fail-closed branch is the entire subject of RFC_017 and was previously reachable only through a live *sql.DB, which is why no test asserted it and the behaviour was documented rather than proven. Extracting verificationDecision makes the ruling table-testable and mutation-provable. The unparseable-spec branch takes the same policy deliberately - it is the same class ('verification could not run'), and exempting it would leave a second silent completion path behind the one this closes.

The flip makes an existing hard-coded message wrong. Before it, only 'defect_persists' could block a completion, so the caller hard-coded the reason as 'post-fix verification found the defect still present' and read its text from payload["detail"]. Once an error can block, that sentence records a finding the verifier never made - and because an error payload carries its text under "error" rather than "detail", the message would also have come out with an empty body. This text is what a human reads off the item's error column, so the two causes must not share a sentence.
Route the two distinct blocking causes to distinct messages and reason codes at the single call site, instead of the hard-coded defect-still-present claim.
edits.sketch:
if !mayComplete {
-		detail, _ := verification["detail"].(string)
-		return failUnverifiedCompletion(ctx, params.DB, itemID, agentType, string(resultJSON),
-			"completion blocked: post-fix verification found the defect still present: "+detail,
-			"verification_failed", logger)
+		msg, reason := blockedCompletionReason(verification)
+		return failUnverifiedCompletion(ctx, params.DB, itemID, agentType, string(resultJSON),
+			msg, reason, logger)

edits.rationale: Assert the ruling so a later session cannot flip the default back by accident rather than by ruling. Mutation-proven, not merely green: restoring the old behaviour (returning true on the error branch) fails exactly the two rows that encode the ruling, and passes again on restore. The table also pins two things a naive implementation gets wrong - that a fail-open opt-in must NOT rescue a persisting defect (it licenses completing when the check could not RUN, never when it ran and said no), and that an error beats a Resolved:true returned alongside it.
edits.sketch: cases: verifier error fails CLOSED by default (mayComplete=false) | fails OPEN only with the explicit opt-in (true) | resolved completes | fail-open policy does NOT rescue a persisting defect (false) | error beats a resolved result returned with it (false); plus blockedCompletionReason must not say 'still present' for an unrunnable verification and must carry the verifier's own text.

edits.rationale: Condition (2) of the platform-seams ordering exemption: a shared seam is registered in the SAME commit that ships it, with its landmine and its open question written down. The landmine is unusually important here because the fact INVERTS - a result._verification.status='error' row used to be a completed item, so every belief formed about that column before today is now wrong in the opposite direction.
edits.sketch: WII-011 - Completion-verifier failure policy (VerifierPolicy.FailOpenOnError, fail-CLOSED default). status BUILT, inert until the next roll. Carries the measurement, the mutation evidence, the LANDMINE, and the named operational cost (three wasted rebuilds per structurally-unanswerable check until empty_section takes 032's stronger option). Index row added in the same commit; count re-grepped and uniqueness checked.

grounded_in: verifiers.go (pre-change): 'ItemVerifier re-checks the defect described by a work item. Returning an error means the verification could not run at all - the caller decides policy (CompleteWorkItemAction fails open and records the error in the result).'

complete_work_item_verification.go (pre-change): 'verifier errors -> fail OPEN (complete, recording the error under result._verification) - discovery re-detection + two-strike is the backstop, and failing closed would wedge items on transient errors'

Live census 2026-08-08, whole life of the gate: SELECT result->'_verification'->>'status', count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE result ? '_verification' GROUP BY 1 -> verified 8, error 2, defect_persists 1. Only 3 of 8 registered verifiers have ever been consulted.

Both errors, verbatim from result._verification.error: 'cannot verify: component a390860e-df2e-4f87-a8df-96405459dad2 no longer exists (genuinely fixed or silently deleted - indistinguishable here)' and the same for a553f25f-c919-48db-932e-0824dad2ee1e. Both items status='complete', attempt_count=0.

bugs_closed/032, its own deferred stronger option: 'if the page still expects that component (a plan_sections entry, a slot reference), absence is not ambiguous at all - it is deletion, and could return Resolved: false.' Both live items meet that condition: pages.sections = ["hero", "featured_article", ...] on pages ai-guides and insights, site 1368e337-dd1d-4799-bbb3-8221a1b79bcc.

The defect is still live: both pages serve a deployed 334-byte component in slot featured-content - '
...

...
' - with no text.

The backstop did not fire: no work item for a featured-content slot has ever existed fleet-wide (item_key LIKE '%featured-content%' -> 0 rows), while findEmptySections' predicate run verbatim against the site returns both components classified empty_heading, locked=f, suppressed=f, build_status='deployed'.

Owner ruling 2026-08-02 (RFC_010, narrowing 2): 'when a seam's widest branch is licensed by "callers must all be X", make X a field with the unsafe default OFF. It costs about four lines, it moves the decision to where a reviewer of the CALLER can see it, and it is the only version that survives a session that did not read the helper. A comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share.'
plan.risks: 1. THE FLIP IS UNIVERSAL AND SILENT AT 8 REGISTRATION SITES. RegisterVerifier keeps its signature, so all 8 verifiers change behaviour without their files being edited. That is the intent (the ruling is a default flip, not a per-verifier migration) but it means 7 verifiers whose error paths have never fired now have an untested consequence. Reviewer should check: does any registered verifier return an error on a case where completing is genuinely the lesser harm? I assert none does today and none opts in, but I have only ever observed 3 of the 8 run. 2. THE NAMED COST: with empty_section's verifier unchanged, its absent-target case now blocks -> item returns to the queue -> page-build-handler REBUILDS THE PAGE, up to max_attempts (3), then failed. For a structurally-unanswerable check that is three wasted LLM rebuilds before a human sees it. RFC_017's option 3 (park without burning attempts) is the structural fix and was explicitly not taken; the cheap per-verifier remedy is bugs_closed/032's stronger option, owned by empty_sections_loop_integrity and told today. 3. A previously-unreachable code path becomes reachable: failUnverifiedCompletion is now called with reason 'verification_unavailable'. Its UPDATE excludes terminal statuses and returns already_flagged_or_terminal on no rows - unchanged by this edit, but now exercised by a second caller. 4. The unparseable-spec branch also flips; if any live item type carries specs this platform cannot parse, those items will now block instead of completing. I did not measure how many specs fail to parse - that is an honest gap, though the branch has produced 0 recorded _verification payloads with 'unparseable spec' in the census. 5. Go change, inert until an image roll; DB config is unaffected. Nothing needs seeding and no migration accompanies it.
